subproblem.title: Squeeze along a filter by approximating families
subproblem.statement: Let l be a filter on a type ι, m : ι → ℝ, a, b : ℕ → ι → ℝ, A, B : ℕ → ℝ and L ∈ ℝ. Suppose that for every k, eventually along l, a_k(i) ≤ m(i) ≤ b_k(i). Suppose also that a_k → A_k and b_k → B_k along l for every k, and that A_k → L and B_k → L as k → ∞. Then m → L along l.
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ {ι : Type} (l : Filter ι) (m : ι → ℝ) (a b : ℕ → ι → ℝ) (A B : ℕ → ℝ) (L : ℝ), (∀ k, ∀ᶠ i in l, a k i ≤ m i ∧ m i ≤ b k i) → (∀ k, Tendsto (a k) l (𝓝 (A k))) → (∀ k, Tendsto (b k) l (𝓝 (B k))) → Tendsto A atTop (𝓝 L) → Tendsto B atTop (𝓝 L) → Tendsto m l (𝓝 L)
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: the ε-argument at the end of step 7 of the parent-supplied proof, stated for general sequences.

1. By Metric.tendsto_nhds it suffices to show: for every ε > 0, eventually along l, |m(i) − L| < ε. Fix ε > 0.

2. Choice of k. Since A_k → L and B_k → L as k → ∞, the properties |A_k − L| < ε/2 and |B_k − L| < ε/2 each hold for all large k. Their conjunction is again eventually true along atTop on ℕ, so it holds for some k ∈ ℕ. Fix such a k.

3. Three eventual facts along l:
 - since a_k → A_k along l, eventually |a_k(i) − A_k| < ε/2;
 - since b_k → B_k along l, eventually |b_k(i) − B_k| < ε/2;
 - by hypothesis, eventually a_k(i) ≤ m(i) ≤ b_k(i).
 A finite intersection of eventual sets is eventual, so all three hold eventually along l.

4. For every such i:
 - m(i) ≥ a_k(i) > A_k − ε/2 > (L − ε/2) − ε/2 = L − ε;
 - m(i) ≤ b_k(i) < B_k + ε/2 < (L + ε/2) + ε/2 = L + ε.
 Hence |m(i) − L| < ε eventually along l.

5. Since ε > 0 was arbitrary, m → L along l. No assumption l ≠ ⊥ is needed: if l = ⊥, every property holds eventually. ∎
proof_key_steps: Given ε > 0, choose one k with |A_k − L| < ε/2 and |B_k − L| < ε/2.
Eventually along l: |a_k(i) − A_k| < ε/2, |b_k(i) − B_k| < ε/2 and a_k(i) ≤ m(i) ≤ b_k(i).
So L − ε < m(i) < L + ε eventually; conclude by Metric.tendsto_nhds.

audit.reason: The type exactly expresses the family-indexed squeeze. The ε/2 proof chooses a common natural-number index and intersects the required eventual conditions. It works for every filter, including the bottom filter, and uses no unstated NeBot assumption.

subproblem.title: Hausdorff measure of balls in an n-plane
subproblem.statement: Let N, n ∈ ℕ, T ∈ G(N,n) (Grassmannian N n) and r > 0. Let P = T.plane ⊆ ℝ^N, an n-dimensional linear subspace, and H^n = μHE[n] on ℝ^N = Euclidean N. Let B_r(0) = closedBall 0 r and B°_r(0) = ball 0 r. Let ω_n = unitBallVolume n, the Lebesgue measure of the open unit ball of ℝ^n = EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin n). Then H^n(P ∩ B_r(0)) = ω_n·r^n and H^n(P ∩ B°_r(0)) = ω_n·r^n in [0,∞]. Precisely, both equal unitBallVolume n * ENNReal.ofReal r ^ n.
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (N n : ℕ) (T : Grassmannian N n) (r : ℝ), 0 < r → (μHE[n] : Measure (Euclidean N)) ((T.plane : Set (Euclidean N)) ∩ closedBall 0 r) = unitBallVolume n * ENNReal.ofReal r ^ n ∧ (μHE[n] : Measure (Euclidean N)) ((T.plane : Set (Euclidean N)) ∩ ball 0 r) = unitBallVolume n * ENNReal.ofReal r ^ n
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: step 6 of the parent-supplied proof (the isometry J and the ball volumes), for an arbitrary radius r > 0.

Notation.
- P := T.plane, a linear subspace of ℝ^N = Euclidean N.
- ℝ^n := EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin n), with Lebesgue measure vol_n = volume.
- H := μHE[n] on ℝ^N.
- In any normed space and for ρ ∈ ℝ, B_ρ(0) = closedBall 0 ρ = {w : ‖w‖ ≤ ρ} and B°_ρ(0) = ball 0 ρ = {w : ‖w‖ < ρ}.

1. An isometric parametrization of P.
 - By Grassmannian.finrank_plane, finrank ℝ P = n.
 - Reindexing stdOrthonormalBasis ℝ P along finCongr (finrank_plane) gives an orthonormal basis b of P indexed by Fin n. Its coordinate map b.repr : P ≃ₗᵢ[ℝ] ℝ^n is a linear isometric equivalence.
 - Let J := P.subtypeₗᵢ ∘ b.repr.symm : ℝ^n → ℝ^N. J is a linear isometry, so ‖J y‖ = ‖y‖ for all y.
 - range J = P: each J y = (b.repr.symm y : P) lies in P, and each w ∈ P equals J(b.repr ⟨w, hw⟩).

2. Measure transfer. Let E ⊆ ℝ^n be any set.
 - H(J(E)) = μHE[n](E) by Isometry.euclideanHausdorffMeasure_image, since J is an isometry.
 - μHE[n] = vol_n on ℝ^n by EuclideanSpace.euclideanHausdorffMeasure_eq_volume n.
 - Hence H(J(E)) = vol_n(E).

3. Balls in P are images of balls. Let A ⊆ ℝ. We claim P ∩ {w ∈ ℝ^N : ‖w‖ ∈ A} = J({y ∈ ℝ^n : ‖y‖ ∈ A}).
 - (⊆) If w ∈ P, then w = J y for some y because range J = P, and ‖y‖ = ‖J y‖ = ‖w‖ ∈ A.
 - (⊇) J y ∈ range J = P and ‖J y‖ = ‖y‖ ∈ A.
 Take A = (−∞, r] and A = (−∞, r). This gives P ∩ B_r(0) = J(B_r(0)) and P ∩ B°_r(0) = J(B°_r(0)), where the balls on the right lie in ℝ^n. By step 2:
  H(P ∩ B_r(0)) = vol_n(B_r(0)) and H(P ∩ B°_r(0)) = vol_n(B°_r(0)).

4. The open ball.
 - vol_n is an additive Haar measure on ℝ^n and r > 0. So Measure.addHaar_ball_of_pos gives vol_n(B°_r(0)) = ofReal(r^{finrank ℝ ℝ^n})·vol_n(B°_1(0)). This lemma needs no nontriviality assumption.
 - finrank ℝ (EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin n)) = n by finrank_euclideanSpace_fin.
 - ofReal(r^n) = ofReal(r)^n because r ≥ 0 (ENNReal.ofReal_pow).
 - vol_n(B°_1(0)) = unitBallVolume n by the definition of unitBallVolume.
 So vol_n(B°_r(0)) = unitBallVolume n · ofReal(r)^n.

5. The closed ball has the same volume: vol_n(B_r(0)) = vol_n(B°_r(0)).
 - If n ≥ 1, then finrank ℝ ℝ^n = n > 0, so ℝ^n is nontrivial (Module.nontrivial_of_finrank_pos). With 0 ≤ r, Measure.addHaar_closedBall and Measure.addHaar_ball both give the value ofReal(r^n)·vol_n(B°_1(0)).
 - If n = 0, ℝ^0 has exactly one point, 0. Since r > 0, we have ‖0‖ = 0 ≤ r and 0 < r, so B_r(0) and B°_r(0) are both the whole space. The sets are equal, hence so are their volumes.

6. Conclusion. By steps 3–5:
 - H(P ∩ B_r(0)) = vol_n(B_r(0)) = vol_n(B°_r(0)) = unitBallVolume n · ofReal(r)^n;
 - H(P ∩ B°_r(0)) = vol_n(B°_r(0)) = unitBallVolume n · ofReal(r)^n. ∎
proof_key_steps: Build a linear isometry J : ℝ^n → ℝ^N with range T.plane from an orthonormal basis of T.plane indexed by Fin n (Grassmannian.finrank_plane).
μHE[n](J(E)) = vol_n(E) for every E ⊆ ℝ^n, by Isometry.euclideanHausdorffMeasure_image and EuclideanSpace.euclideanHausdorffMeasure_eq_volume.
T.plane ∩ B_r(0) = J(B_r(0)) and T.plane ∩ B°_r(0) = J(B°_r(0)), since J preserves norms and has range T.plane.
vol_n(B°_r(0)) = unitBallVolume n · ofReal(r)^n by Measure.addHaar_ball_of_pos (r > 0), finrank = n and ofReal_pow.
vol_n(B_r(0)) = vol_n(B°_r(0)): by addHaar_closedBall and addHaar_ball when n ≥ 1; for n = 0 both balls are the whole one-point space.

audit.reason: The one-line type matches both ENNReal-valued ball identities and every hypothesis. The proof constructs the required isometry, transfers Hausdorff measure, and computes the volumes. Its separate n=0 argument correctly avoids a nontriviality assumption. It is complete and independent.

subproblem.title: Cut-off sandwich for the rescaled ball integral
subproblem.statement:
Let V be an n-varifold on U ⊆ ℝ^N (Varifold N n U), x ∈ ℝ^N, β : G(N,n) → ℝ continuous with β ≥ 0, k ∈ ℕ, and r > 0 with B_{2r}(x) ⊆ U (closed ball). Let φ_k⁺(y) = max(0, 1 − (k+1)·max(0, ‖y‖ − 1)) and φ_k⁻(y) = min(1, (k+1)·max(0, 1 − ‖y‖)), and let V_{x,r} = rescaledMeasure V x r. Then
∫ φ_k⁻(y)β(S) dV_{x,r}(y,S) ≤ (∫_{B_r(x)×G(N,n)} β(S) dV(y,S)) / r^n ≤ ∫ φ_k⁺(y)β(S) dV_{x,r}(y,S).
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (N n : ℕ) (U : Set (Euclidean N)) (V : Varifold N n U) (x : Euclidean N) (β : C(Grassmannian N n, ℝ)) (r : ℝ) (k : ℕ), 0 < r → closedBall x (2 * r) ⊆ U → (∀ S, 0 ≤ β S) → (∫ z, min 1 (((k : ℝ) + 1) * max 0 (1 - ‖z.1‖)) * β z.2 ∂(rescaledMeasure V x r)) ≤ (∫ z in closedBall x r ×ˢ (univ : Set (Grassmannian N n)), β z.2 ∂V.measure) / r ^ n ∧ (∫ z in closedBall x r ×ˢ (univ : Set (Grassmannian N n)), β z.2 ∂V.measure) / r ^ n ≤ ∫ z, max 0 (1 - ((k : ℝ) + 1) * max 0 (‖z.1‖ - 1)) * β z.2 ∂(rescaledMeasure V x r)
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: steps 2, 3, 5 (items (5a), (5c)) and the first display of step 7 of the parent-supplied proof: monotonicity of the integral after the change of variables, at one fixed radius r. The index k is replaced by k + 1.

Notation.
- G := Grassmannian N n, a compact space.
- a := k + 1 ≥ 1. For w ∈ ℝ^N, φ⁺(w) := max(0, 1 − a·max(0, ‖w‖ − 1)) and φ⁻(w) := min(1, a·max(0, 1 − ‖w‖)).
- Φ(y,S) := (r⁻¹(y − x), S). By definition, rescaledMeasure V x r = c • (V.measure.map Φ) with c := ofReal(r⁻¹^n).
- B := B_r(x) × G and K := B_{2r}(x) × G (closed balls).
- ‖β‖ := sup_S |β(S)| < ∞, since G is compact; so |β(S)| ≤ ‖β‖ for all S (ContinuousMap.norm_coe_le_norm).

1. Finite mass on K. B_{2r}(x) is a closed ball in ℝ^N, hence compact, and B_{2r}(x) ⊆ U by hypothesis. So V.measure(K) < ∞ by the varifold axiom finite_on_compact.

2. Cut-off facts, for all w (as in the parent's step 5):
 - 0 ≤ φ^± ≤ 1;
 - φ⁺(w) = 1 if ‖w‖ ≤ 1, since then max(0, ‖w‖ − 1) = 0;
 - φ⁺(w) = 0 if ‖w‖ > 2, since then a(‖w‖ − 1) > 1;
 - φ⁻(w) = 0 if ‖w‖ > 1, since then max(0, 1 − ‖w‖) = 0;
 - φ^± are continuous.

3. Geometry of Φ. Since r > 0, ‖Φ(y,S).1‖ = ‖r⁻¹(y − x)‖ = ‖y − x‖/r. Hence:
 - (y,S) ∈ B ⟺ ‖y − x‖ ≤ r ⟺ ‖Φ(y,S).1‖ ≤ 1;
 - if (y,S) ∉ K, then ‖y − x‖ > 2r, so ‖Φ(y,S).1‖ > 2.

4. Change of variables. For every continuous g : ℝ^N × G → ℝ,
  ∫ g d(rescaledMeasure V x r) = r⁻¹^n · ∫ g∘Φ dV.measure.
 - integral_smul_measure gives ∫ g d(c•ν) = c.toReal · ∫ g dν for every g. Since r⁻¹^n ≥ 0, c.toReal = r⁻¹^n.
 - Φ is continuous, hence measurable, and g is continuous, hence a.e.-strongly measurable for V.measure.map Φ. So integral_map gives ∫ g d(V.measure.map Φ) = ∫ g∘Φ dV.measure.
 Neither identity needs integrability.

5. The middle term. B is measurable (closed ball × univ), so integral_indicator gives ∫_B β(S) dV = ∫ 1_B(y,S)β(S) dV(y,S). Also (r^n)⁻¹ = r⁻¹^n. Hence
  (∫_B β(S) dV)/r^n = r⁻¹^n · ∫ h_B dV, where h_B(y,S) := 1_B(y,S)·β(S).

6. Integrability. Let h be a.e.-strongly measurable with |h| ≤ ‖β‖ everywhere and h = 0 outside K. Then h is integrable on K (bounded on a set of finite measure: Measure.integrableOn_of_bounded with step 1), and it vanishes off K, so h is V.measure-integrable (IntegrableOn.integrable_of_forall_notMem_eq_zero). This applies to three functions:
 - h⁻(y,S) := φ⁻(Φ(y,S).1)·β(S) and h⁺(y,S) := φ⁺(Φ(y,S).1)·β(S). Both are continuous, and |h^±| ≤ 1·‖β‖ by step 2. Off K we have ‖Φ.1‖ > 2 > 1, so φ^±(Φ.1) = 0 by step 2.
 - h_B. It is the indicator of a measurable set times a continuous function, and |h_B| ≤ ‖β‖. Off K the point is not in B, since ‖Φ.1‖ > 2 > 1 (step 3), so h_B = 0.

7. Pointwise sandwich: h⁻ ≤ h_B ≤ h⁺ everywhere.
 - If (y,S) ∈ B: h_B = β(S). Since ‖Φ.1‖ ≤ 1, φ⁺(Φ.1) = 1, so h⁺ = β(S). Also h⁻ = φ⁻(Φ.1)·β(S) ≤ 1·β(S), because φ⁻ ≤ 1 and β(S) ≥ 0.
 - If (y,S) ∉ B: h_B = 0. Since ‖Φ.1‖ > 1, φ⁻(Φ.1) = 0, so h⁻ = 0. And h⁺ = φ⁺(Φ.1)·β(S) ≥ 0, as both factors are ≥ 0.

8. Conclusion.
 - By step 6 and integral_mono, ∫ h⁻ dV ≤ ∫ h_B dV ≤ ∫ h⁺ dV. Multiplying by r⁻¹^n ≥ 0 preserves both inequalities.
 - Apply step 4 to the continuous functions g^±(y,S) := φ^±(y)·β(S). Φ does not change the second coordinate, so g^±∘Φ = h^±. Hence r⁻¹^n · ∫ h^± dV = ∫ φ^±(y)β(S) d(rescaledMeasure V x r)(y,S).
 - By step 5, the middle term is (∫_{B_r(x)×G} β(S) dV)/r^n.
 Together these give both inequalities. ∎
proof_key_steps: V(B_{2r}(x)×G) < ∞, since B_{2r}(x) is compact and contained in U (finite_on_compact).
Change of variables: ∫ g dV_{x,r} = r⁻¹^n ∫ g∘Φ dV for continuous g (integral_smul_measure, integral_map).
Middle term: (∫_{B_r(x)×G} β dV)/r^n = r⁻¹^n ∫ 1_{B_r(x)×G}·β dV (integral_indicator).
All three integrands are bounded by ‖β‖ and vanish off B_{2r}(x)×G, hence are integrable.
Pointwise φ⁻(Φ.1)β ≤ 1_Bβ ≤ φ⁺(Φ.1)β, because β ≥ 0 and ‖Φ.1‖ ≤ 1 ⟺ (y,S) ∈ B; integrate and multiply by r⁻¹^n ≥ 0.

subproblem.title: Plane integrals of the unit-ball cut-offs converge to ω_n
subproblem.statement: Let N, n ∈ ℕ and T ∈ G(N,n). For k ∈ ℕ and y ∈ ℝ^N put φ_k⁺(y) = max(0, 1 − (k+1)·max(0, ‖y‖ − 1)) and φ_k⁻(y) = min(1, (k+1)·max(0, 1 − ‖y‖)). Then, as k → ∞, ∫_{T.plane} φ_k⁺ dH^n → ω_n and ∫_{T.plane} φ_k⁻ dH^n → ω_n. Here H^n = μHE[n] on ℝ^N, the integrals are real Bochner integrals over T.plane (with respect to μHE[n] restricted to T.plane), and ω_n = (unitBallVolume n).toReal.
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (N n : ℕ) (T : Grassmannian N n), Tendsto (fun k : ℕ ↦ ∫ y in (T.plane : Set (Euclidean N)), max 0 (1 - ((k : ℝ) + 1) * max 0 (‖y‖ - 1)) ∂(μHE[n] : Measure (Euclidean N))) atTop (𝓝 (unitBallVolume n).toReal) ∧ Tendsto (fun k : ℕ ↦ ∫ y in (T.plane : Set (Euclidean N)), min 1 (((k : ℝ) + 1) * max 0 (1 - ‖y‖)) ∂(μHE[n] : Measure (Euclidean N))) atTop (𝓝 (unitBallVolume n).toReal)
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: step 5 (the cut-offs, items (5a)–(5b)) and step 6 (dominated convergence) of the parent-supplied proof. The index k is replaced by k + 1, so every k ∈ ℕ is allowed.

Notation.
- P := T.plane and H := μHE[n] on ℝ^N.
- μ := H restricted to P, a measure on ℝ^N. By definition of the set integral, ∫_P f dH = ∫ f dμ.
- For k ∈ ℕ put a_k := k + 1 ≥ 1. For y ∈ ℝ^N with s := ‖y‖, put φ_k⁺(y) := max(0, 1 − a_k·max(0, s − 1)) and φ_k⁻(y) := min(1, a_k·max(0, 1 − s)).
- ω := (unitBallVolume n).toReal.

1. Masses of balls under μ.
 - unitBallVolume n = vol_n(B°_1(0)) < ∞, because Lebesgue measure on the proper space ℝ^n is locally finite and gives balls finite mass (measure_ball_lt_top).
 - Let ρ > 0. Closed and open balls are measurable, so μ(B_ρ(0)) = H(B_ρ(0) ∩ P) = H(P ∩ B_ρ(0)), and likewise μ(B°_ρ(0)) = H(P ∩ B°_ρ(0)).
 - By the sibling plane_ball_measure, both equal unitBallVolume n · ofReal(ρ)^n.
 - Hence μ(B_2(0)) = unitBallVolume n · ofReal(2)^n < ∞. Since ofReal(1)^n = 1, also μ(B_1(0)) = μ(B°_1(0)) = unitBallVolume n.

2. Dominating function. Let g := 1_{B_2(0)}, the indicator of the closed ball of radius 2 with value 1. The constant 1 is integrable on B_2(0) because μ(B_2(0)) < ∞ (step 1). Since B_2(0) is measurable, g is μ-integrable (integrable_indicator_iff).

3. Elementary properties, for every k and y (with s = ‖y‖):
 (a) 0 ≤ φ_k⁺(y) ≤ 1. It is a max with 0, and 1 − a_k·max(0, s − 1) ≤ 1 because a_k ≥ 0 and max(0, s − 1) ≥ 0.
 (b) 0 ≤ φ_k⁻(y) ≤ 1. It is a min with 1, and a_k·max(0, 1 − s) ≥ 0.
 (c) If s > 2, then φ_k⁺(y) = 0. Indeed max(0, s − 1) = s − 1 > 1 and a_k ≥ 1, so a_k(s − 1) > 1 and 1 − a_k(s − 1) < 0.
 (d) If s ≥ 1, then φ_k⁻(y) = 0, because max(0, 1 − s) = 0.
 (e) φ_k^± are continuous, being built from the norm, constants, products, max and min. Hence they are a.e.-strongly measurable.
 From (a)–(d), |φ_k^±(y)| ≤ g(y) for all y: if s ≤ 2 then g(y) = 1, and if s > 2 then φ_k^±(y) = 0.

4. Pointwise limits as k → ∞, for every y (with s = ‖y‖).
 (a) φ_k⁺(y) → 1_{B_1(0)}(y).
  - If s ≤ 1, then max(0, s − 1) = 0, so φ_k⁺(y) = max(0, 1) = 1 = 1_{B_1(0)}(y) for every k.
  - If s > 1, choose k₀ ∈ ℕ with k₀ > 1/(s − 1). For k ≥ k₀, a_k(s − 1) ≥ (k₀ + 1)(s − 1) > 1, so φ_k⁺(y) = 0 = 1_{B_1(0)}(y).
  In both cases the sequence is eventually equal to its limit.
 (b) φ_k⁻(y) → 1_{B°_1(0)}(y).
  - If s < 1, choose k₀ ∈ ℕ with k₀ > 1/(1 − s). For k ≥ k₀, a_k(1 − s) ≥ 1, so φ_k⁻(y) = min(1, a_k(1 − s)) = 1 = 1_{B°_1(0)}(y).
  - If s ≥ 1, then φ_k⁻(y) = 0 = 1_{B°_1(0)}(y) for every k.

5. Dominated convergence. Apply tendsto_integral_of_dominated_convergence with the bound g from step 2, measurability from 3(e), domination from step 3 and the limits from step 4. As k → ∞:
  ∫ φ_k⁺ dμ → ∫ 1_{B_1(0)} dμ and ∫ φ_k⁻ dμ → ∫ 1_{B°_1(0)} dμ.

6. Value of the limits. For a measurable set A, ∫ 1_A dμ = ∫_A 1 dμ = μ.real(A) = (μ(A)).toReal (integral_indicator and setIntegral_const). By step 1, (μ(B_1(0))).toReal = (μ(B°_1(0))).toReal = (unitBallVolume n).toReal = ω. Since ∫ φ dμ is ∫_{T.plane} φ dμHE[n], both limits in the statement hold. ∎
proof_key_steps: Under μ = μHE[n]⌞T.plane, μ(B_2(0)) < ∞ and μ(B_1(0)) = μ(B°_1(0)) = unitBallVolume n, by sibling plane_ball_measure and unitBallVolume n < ∞ (measure_ball_lt_top).
The cut-offs are continuous with |φ_k^±| ≤ 1_{B_2(0)}, and this indicator is μ-integrable.
Pointwise, φ_k⁺ → 1_{B_1(0)} and φ_k⁻ → 1_{B°_1(0)}; each sequence is eventually constant in k.
Dominated convergence: the limits are ∫1_{B_1(0)} dμ = ∫1_{B°_1(0)} dμ = (unitBallVolume n).toReal.

audit.reason: The type exactly matches both k+1 cutoff limits. The declared plane_ball_measure dependency supplies finite dominating mass and equal open/closed unit-ball masses. Measurability, domination, pointwise limits, and evaluation of both limiting integrals are justified without circularity.

subproblem.title: Ball-integral limit at a flat blow-up for β ≥ 0
subproblem.statement:
Let V be an n-varifold on an open U ⊆ ℝ^N, x ∈ U, T ∈ G(N,n) and θ ∈ ℝ. Let l be a filter on a type ι and t : ι → ℝ with t_i → 0 within (0,∞) along l. Suppose that for every f ∈ C_c(ℝ^N × G(N,n)), ∫ f dV_{x,t_i} → θ ∫ f dv(T) along l, where V_{x,r} = rescaledMeasure V x r and v(T) = planeVarifoldMeasure T. Then for every continuous β : G(N,n) → ℝ with β ≥ 0,
(∫_{B_{t_i}(x)×G(N,n)} β(S) dV(y,S)) / t_i^n → θ·ω_n·β(T) along l,
where B_r(x) is the closed ball and ω_n = (unitBallVolume n).toReal.
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (N n : ℕ) (U : Set (Euclidean N)) (V : Varifold N n U) (x : Euclidean N) (T : Grassmannian N n) (θ : ℝ) {ι : Type} (l : Filter ι) (t : ι → ℝ), x ∈ U → Tendsto t l (𝓝[>] 0) → (∀ f : C_c(Euclidean N × Grassmannian N n, ℝ), Tendsto (fun i ↦ ∫ z, f z ∂(rescaledMeasure V x (t i))) l (𝓝 (θ * ∫ z, f z ∂(planeVarifoldMeasure T)))) → ∀ β : C(Grassmannian N n, ℝ), (∀ S, 0 ≤ β S) → Tendsto (fun i ↦ (∫ z in closedBall x (t i) ×ˢ (univ : Set (Grassmannian N n)), β z.2 ∂V.measure) / t i ^ n) l (𝓝 (θ * (unitBallVolume n).toReal * β T))
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: steps 2, 4, 5 and 7 of the parent-supplied proof (the case β ≥ 0), with k replaced by k + 1. The siblings supply three ingredients:
- rescaled_sandwich: the sandwich inequalities;
- plane_cutoff_limits: the cut-off limits on the plane;
- filter_squeeze: the ε-argument.

Notation.
- G := Grassmannian N n, which is compact (Grassmannian.instCompactSpace).
- V_r := rescaledMeasure V x r and ω := (unitBallVolume n).toReal.
- For k ∈ ℕ and y ∈ ℝ^N: φ_k⁺(y) := max(0, 1 − (k+1)·max(0, ‖y‖ − 1)) and φ_k⁻(y) := min(1, (k+1)·max(0, 1 − ‖y‖)).
- Fix a continuous β : G → ℝ with β ≥ 0, and put m(i) := (∫_{B_{t_i}(x)×G} β(S) dV)/t_i^n.

1. Good radii.
 - U is open (V.isOpen_domain) and x ∈ U, so there is ε > 0 with B°_ε(x) ⊆ U (Metric.isOpen_iff).
 - The interval (0, ε/2) belongs to the filter 𝓝[>] 0 (Ioo_mem_nhdsGT). Since t → 0 within (0,∞) along l, eventually along l we have 0 < t_i < ε/2.
 - For such i, B_{2t_i}(x) ⊆ B°_ε(x) ⊆ U, because 2t_i < ε.

2. Cut-off facts. φ_k^± are continuous, and both vanish whenever ‖y‖ > 2:
 - for φ_k⁺: max(0, ‖y‖ − 1) = ‖y‖ − 1 > 1 and k + 1 ≥ 1, so 1 − (k+1)(‖y‖ − 1) < 0;
 - for φ_k⁻: max(0, 1 − ‖y‖) = 0.

3. Test functions. For φ ∈ {φ_k⁺, φ_k⁻} define F_φ(y,S) := φ(y)·β(S).
 - F_φ is continuous on ℝ^N × G.
 - By step 2, F_φ vanishes outside B_2(0) × G. This set is compact, as the product of a closed ball of ℝ^N and the compact space G.
 Hence F_φ has compact support (HasCompactSupport.intro), so F_φ ∈ C_c(ℝ^N × G, ℝ).

4. Plane side. planeVarifoldMeasure T is the image of μHE[n]⌞T.plane under the measurable map y ↦ (y,T), and F_φ is continuous. So integral_map gives
  ∫ F_φ d(planeVarifoldMeasure T) = ∫ F_φ(y,T) d(μHE[n]⌞T.plane)(y) = ∫_{T.plane} φ(y)·β(T) dμHE[n] = c(φ)·β(T),
 where c(φ) := ∫_{T.plane} φ dμHE[n] and the last step is integral_mul_const. Write c_k^± := c(φ_k^±).

5. Limits along l for fixed k. Apply the hypothesis to F_{φ_k⁻} and F_{φ_k⁺} and use step 4. Along l:
  a_k(i) := ∫ φ_k⁻(y)β(S) dV_{t_i}(y,S) → A_k := θ·(c_k⁻·β(T)),
  b_k(i) := ∫ φ_k⁺(y)β(S) dV_{t_i}(y,S) → B_k := θ·(c_k⁺·β(T)).
 Here ∫ F_φ dV_{t_i} is literally ∫ φ(y)β(S) dV_{t_i}(y,S), since F_φ is defined by that formula.

6. Limits in k. By the sibling plane_cutoff_limits, c_k⁺ → ω and c_k⁻ → ω as k → ∞. Multiplication by the constants β(T) and θ is continuous, so A_k → θ(ωβ(T)) and B_k → θ(ωβ(T)). Note θ(ωβ(T)) = θ·ω·β(T).

7. Sandwich. Fix k. Take any i with 0 < t_i < ε/2; this holds eventually along l by step 1. The sibling rescaled_sandwich applies with r := t_i, because 0 < t_i, B_{2t_i}(x) ⊆ U and β ≥ 0. It gives a_k(i) ≤ m(i) ≤ b_k(i). Hence for every k, eventually along l, a_k(i) ≤ m(i) ≤ b_k(i).

8. Conclusion. Apply the sibling filter_squeeze with the filter l, the sequence m, the families a and b, the numbers A_k and B_k, and L := θ·ω·β(T), using steps 5, 6 and 7. It gives m → θ·ω·β(T) along l. The sign of θ plays no role. ∎
proof_key_steps: Eventually 0 < t_i < ε/2, where B°_ε(x) ⊆ U; hence B_{2t_i}(x) ⊆ U.
F_k^±(y,S) = φ_k^±(y)β(S) are continuous and supported in the compact set B_2(0)×G, so they belong to C_c(ℝ^N × G).
∫F_k^± dv(T) = β(T)·∫_{T.plane} φ_k^± dH^n (integral_map); the hypothesis gives a_k → θc_k⁻β(T) and b_k → θc_k⁺β(T) along l.
Sibling plane_cutoff_limits: c_k^± → ω, so A_k → θωβ(T) and B_k → θωβ(T).
Sibling rescaled_sandwich: eventually a_k(i) ≤ m(i) ≤ b_k(i); then sibling filter_squeeze gives m → θωβ(T).
